prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every truck-accident case — the best attorney for you depends on the specifics of your crash, injuries, and what you want (maximum recovery, quick settlement, or trial). I can help you find a lawyer, but here are practical steps and what to look for so you pick the best one for your situation.

What to look for in a truck-accident lawyer
- Substantial truck-specific experience: look for attorneys who handle commercial vehicle cases often (FMCSA rules, driver logs, maintenance records, hours-of-service violations, insurance issues).  
- Trial experience and results: trucking insurers frequently fight hard; attorneys who try cases when needed typically get better settlements.  
- Firm resources: truck cases require accident reconstructionists, retained experts, and the ability to fund discovery and expert fees.  
- Board certification or recognized peer-review ratings: Texas Board of Legal Specialization certification in Personal Injury Trial Law, “AV” ratings (Martindale-Hubbell), Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, etc., are useful indicators.  
- Transparent fee structure and communication style: ask how they’ll communicate, who will handle day-to-day work, and whether they take cases on contingency.  
- Local knowledge: familiarity with Dallas courts, judges, and local medical providers helps.

Key questions to ask at a consultation
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases against (or defended) major carriers/insurers? Any notable outcomes?  
- What investigators and experts will you use? Who pays those costs up front?  
- What is your fee (typical contingency %), and what costs would I be responsible for?  
- Who in your office will be my main contact and how often will I get updates?  
- What is your strategy for my type of case? Estimated timeline and value range?  
- Do you handle medical liens and health insurance subrogation?

Practical things to preserve now
- Preserve your phone (photos/texts), photos of the scene/vehicles/injuries, witness contacts, the police report number, employer and insurance info for the truck driver, and any medical records/bills. Don’t post details to social media. Act quickly — trucking companies often destroy/overwrite driver logs and electronic data unless told not to.

Timing and legal limits
- Texas personal-injury statute of limitations is generally 2 years from the date of injury. Trucking evidence can disappear quickly, so contact an attorney early.

Where to search and verify attorneys
- Dallas Bar Association referral service  
- Texas Trial Lawyers Association member lists  
- Martindale-Hubbell (ratings), Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, AVVO — check peer and client reviews  
- Texas Bar website to confirm license/sanctions

Typical fees
- Common contingency fees range ~33% for pre-suit/settlement and may be higher if the case goes to trial (sometimes up to 40% or more negotiated). Ask how costs are handled if you don’t recover.

If you’d like, I can:
- Help you draft a short script or email to send to potential attorneys.  
- Create a prioritized list of specific questions for consultations.  
- If you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood in Dallas and a few details about the crash (date, injuries, whether the truck was a commercial vehicle, whether you’ve seen a doctor), I can suggest what types of firms to contact and a checklist of documents to have ready.

Would you like me to draft a consultation script or help you prepare a short intake to send to several Dallas firms?
